rationale: Evidence across cohort studies and comprehensive reviews indicates a bimodal phenotypic distribution in FDXR-associated disease (OMIM #620887). Features including microcephaly (both primary and secondary) and elevated plasma/CSF lactate or basal ganglia MRS lactate peaks occur predominantly in severe infantile-onset encephalopathy, neurodevelopmental regression, and Leigh-like presentations. In contrast, patients presenting with juvenile- or adult-onset isolated auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy generally do not demonstrate early infantile microcephaly or chronic baseline lactic acidemia, though acute metabolic crises with lactate elevation can occasionally be triggered during intercurrent physiological stress or infection.

evidence.text: FDXR deficiency exhibits a broad clinical spectrum ranging from Leigh syndrome with early demise and severe infantile-onset encephalopathy accompanied by microcephaly and elevated CSF lactate, to milder movement disorders and isolated optic/acoustic neuropathy.

new_directions.question_text: Does intermittent or infection-provoked metabolic testing in juvenile-onset isolated sensory neuropathy cases uncover latent subclinical lactic acidemia or MRS lactate peaks?
new_directions.rationale: While baseline lactate and microcephaly are restricted to the early encephalopathic Leigh-like subtype, acute catabolic or infectious triggers have been shown to induce sudden neuroimaging abnormalities with basal ganglia lactate peaks in previously asymptomatic young patients.

new_directions.question_text: What specific biochemical threshold of residual ferredoxin reductase oxidoreductase activity dictates the boundary between isolated optic-acoustic neuropathy and severe Leigh syndrome?
new_directions.rationale: Over 80% of reported mutations are missense variants whose residual Fe-S cluster biosynthesis capacity likely determines whether development is spared (permitting normal head circumference) or severely disrupted during embryogenesis/infancy.
